title: A Phase II, prospective, single-center study of FAPI PET imaging and liquid biopsy in bladder cancer
official: Phase II, interventional, prospective, non-randomized, single-center clinical trial to stage bladder cancer and support clinical decision-making using fibroblast activation protein–alpha inhibitor (FAPI) PET imaging and liquid biopsy
summary: Main objective: Assessing the diagnostic accuracy of FAPI PET and liquid biopsy in bladder cancer staging vs conventional imaging
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.Participant is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study; 2.Men and women with diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma (high-grade NMIBC or MIBC); 3.Age≥18; 4.ECOG performance status < 2; 5.Ability to undergo imaging study procedures and blood/urine collection; 6.For males and females of reproductive potential: use of highly effective contraceptionmethods as defined by the “CTCG Recommendation related to contraception andpregnancy testing in clinical trials”, from the screening until 1 week after study drugadministration. 7.For patients eligible to subcohort 1: availability of baseline FAPI PET and liquid biopsybefore the start of systemic treatment for bladder cancer
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.Pregnant or breast-feeding women; 2.Systemic treatment for other oncological diseases in the previous two years; 3.Previous systemic or locoregional treatments (TURB excluded) for bladder cancer; thiscriterion does not apply to patients eligible for subcohort 1;4. Any condition such as severe claustrophobia or severe uncontrolled psychiatric disorders which in the opinion of investigators makes it undesirable for the patient to participate in the study or which could jeopardize compliance with the protocol, 5. Participation in other clinical trials is not per se exclusionary; however, subjects enrolled in another interventional study may be excluded if concurrent participation is considered by the investigator or sponsor to potentially impact subject safety, protocol compliance, or interpretation of study results
